title: Harden queue and rerun evidence
summary: Make rerun current-state evidence independent from bounded history, harden per-file scanning and Network claim correlation, add a configurable queue-snapshot freshness window, remove the dead normal-queue rerun fallback, and disclose the evidence boundaries in the WebView and route documentation.
reason: A fixed history cap and broad manifest-state inference could hide live local work, describe an unverified Network batch as active, or suppress readable history after one file error. Blank Run Once also used only a fixed file-age check, while obsolete queue fallback code preserved a second rerun projection path.
behavior_before: Local current rerun selection was limited by recent history, manifest scans could fail as a group, Network activity did not require a fresh exact persisted claim, queue-snapshot authority used a fixed 60-second mtime check, and the normal queue retained an unused rerun-manifest fallback implementation.
behavior_after: Local live reruns are selected through exact ActiveJobs correlation outside the history cap; history reports bounded loaded/discovered counts and per-file warnings; Network active state requires exact fresh coordinator claim evidence; queue-snapshot authority validates produced_at and mtime against QueueLaunchSnapshotFreshnessSeconds; the normal queue has one projection path and the WebView labels bounded/unverified evidence explicitly.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_process_launch.py: produced_at age, clock skew, file age, and configured freshness
tests/python/desktop/test_process_rerun_results.py: live lookup outside history, resilient scanning, history-window counts, exact Network claims, unverified Network state, and ambiguity
